content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-science-speed","title":"Speed = Distance ÷ Time","quick":"Speed tells how fast something moves. It is found by dividing the distance covered by the time taken. Units must match, like km and hours.","full":"Speed means how much distance is covered in a given time. Think of a bus going from home to the market: if the bus covers 20 km in 1 hour, its speed is 20 km/h. Step by step: take the total distance travelled, divide it by the total time taken, and you get speed. If distance is in km and time is in hours, speed comes in km/h. Average speed is used when speed is not exactly constant throughout the trip, so we just divide total distance by total time taken, ignoring small speed-ups or slow-downs on the way. Children often confuse speed with distance or time alone — speed is a rate, it combines both.","traps":["Forgetting to divide and just writing distance or time as the answer","Mixing units like km with minutes without converting","Not writing the unit (km/h) with the final answer"],"misconception":"Child thinks speed is just the distance number, not realizing it must be divided by time.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If a bus goes 100 km in 2 hours, what is its speed?","expected_answer_hint":"50 km/h, found by dividing 100 by 2"},{"q":"Why do we write 'km/h' and not just a number for speed?","expected_answer_hint":"Because speed shows distance covered per hour, so unit shows both distance and time"}],"check_question":{"q":"A cyclist travels 60 km in 3 hours.
